newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila to penalise non-performing telephone firms.
newsitem.headline: Manila to penalise non-performing telephone firms.

text.p: The Philippine transportation and communication department said on Wednesday it will penalise telephone firms which failed to install at least 80 percent of lines they had agreed to lay.

Communications secretary Amado Lagdameo directed National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) head Simeon Kintanar in a memorandum to "impose appropriate penalties/sanctions commensurate to the level of non-compliance of carriers..."
Kintanar earlier said performance bonds of the firms may be confiscated or permits may be cancelled.
Under an executive order, cellular operators such as Pilipino Telephone Corp and Express Telecommunications Co Inc are required to install 400,000 lines each.

International gateway facility (IGF) operators such as Capitol Wireless Inc, Eastern Telecommunications Philippines Inc, Digital Telecommunications Philippines Inc, and ICC Telecoms have to install 300,000 lines each.
Globe Telecom, Smart Communications Co Inc and Isla Communications Co Inc are required to put up 700,000 lines each as cellular and IGF operators.
Lagdameo said that of the three-year compliance period, the telecom firms have only one year and a half to put up their committed telephone lines.
The government had taken these commitments on laying new land lines in exchange for licences to run lucrative cellular telephone and international gateway services.
